Contract review — **PASS** — PR #8159 (objectui#7698), head `5d68aecbb`

Reviewed-by: `domain:ui` @ objectui PM seat, `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`, in-seat at **`opus` = `TIER_DEFAULT`**. `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`claude-fable-5-1`) is measured unavailable (429). ⛔ Not described as running at contract-review tier.

## ⭐ The Zone-2 clause worked: the correction I handed over was itself incomplete

My dispatch handed the dev comment 5550238143's mark-component table **explicitly as the previous seat's reading, ⛔ not as fact**, and told it to rebuild the census with its own lit control. It did — and found the correction short.

Re-measured by this seat on `origin/main`, `cmp?.` call sites in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`:

```
:1832  Scatter        fillOpacity only
:1898  Line  (combo)  strokeOpacity + strokeDasharray
:1905  Area  (combo)  all three
:1911  Bar   (combo)  fillOpacity only
:2037  Bar            fillOpacity only
:2048  Line           strokeOpacity + strokeDasharray
:2056  Area           all three
```

⇒ **seven**, not the card's five (with stale numbers) and not the correction's four. The correction omitted both **Line** sites and **Area `:1905`**. ⭐ Three successive readings of the same file, each closer; the one that held is the one taken with a control rather than inherited.

The mechanism claim also confirmed at `:96`: `s.dashArray ?? (kind === 'line' || kind === 'area' ? '4 4' : undefined)` — the `??` takes the left side **whatever the kind**, so an authored dash was returned for bar and scatter too and then dropped **at the mark**. ⭐ And the dev proved that with a *lit control rather than a reading*: against the pre-fix implementation the comparison-bar pin reports `fillOpacity '0.4'` **present** and `strokeDasharray` **null** — the two channels diverging at one call site is what makes "the mark owns the drop" a measurement instead of an inference.

## ① Derived judgments

**Clause-②: NO, verified.** The `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` diff is **entirely inside JSDoc block comments** — `opacity?: number;` and `dashArray?: string;` are byte-identical, and no spec or mirror member moves. Hence `@object-ui/types: patch`, which is the honest minimum for a comments-only change. `@object-ui/plugin-charts: minor` for the behaviour. ✅

**Option A implemented as adjudicated, and both halves closed.** `comparisonStyle` → `seriesStyle`, no longer returning `null` off a comparison series, so an authored key applies whatever the `variant`; the muted **defaults** stay gated on `variant === 'comparison'`. And the Bar and Scatter marks now pass `strokeOpacity` / `strokeDasharray`, closing the half the card's body located in the wrong place.

**⭐⭐ The sharpest thing in this PR, and it is a defect the fix could easily have introduced.** The old helper computed `strokeOpacity` for bar (`0.6`) and scatter (`0.5`) — values **no mark ever consumed**, because this renderer strokes neither family. Opening `strokeOpacity` on those marks would therefore have handed them a default they never had, **newly muting every comparison bar and scatter stroke**. The dev spotted it and spelled those two `undefined`, then pinned exactly that:

> *「gives a comparison bar NO dash and NO stroke fade — the defaults are per family, and the marks that just gained these props must not inherit one」*

⇒ **opening a channel can leak a previously-inert default.** That is not in the card, not in triage, and not in my dispatch. It is the kind of thing that ships as "a small visual regression nobody can explain".

## ② semver and read-coupling

`minor` + `patch`, `major` forbidden, `Changeset Bump Policy` green. ✅

**The read-coupling my dispatch made binding is satisfied in BOTH places** — PR #7684's interim "comparison-only" wording is removed from the `plugin-charts.mdx` table rows **and** from the `ChartDataSeries` mirror JSDoc. objectui#7070's rule (restated, ⛔ not left to rot) is met, and the replacement wording is more precise than a simple deletion: it distinguishes *「the key is unconditional」* from *「only a stroked mark can show a dash — the mark's geometry, not a condition on the key」*. ⭐ That asymmetry is real and would have been easy to paper over.

## ③ Boundary flags

- **The pins render through `ChartRenderer` and read the DOM, ⛔ not `seriesStyle` directly** — with the reason stated: *「the defect was a value surviving normalization and then dying at the mark: only the DOM says whether the mark applied it」*. ⭐ A unit test on the helper would have passed against the broken tree.
- ⭐ `paint()` treats `null` — the DOM's answer for an absent attribute — as **a real reading**, and several pins assert exactly that. That is what lets "no default leaked" be asserted rather than assumed.
- ⭐ **One pin names the second gap explicitly**: *「reaches a COMPARISON bar mark (a fix at the `variant` guard alone would not)」*. It is the case that fails for a **different reason** than the primary-series cases, and it is pinned separately for that reason.
- **Ablation: 8 of 13 failed, and the 5 that passed are exactly the regression pins.** Mutation proven on disk before the run — working blob equal to the pre-fix blob `63a5e34c9` and different from `HEAD`'s `ae52b1d01`, with anchored counts moving `seriesStyle` 6→0 and `comparisonStyle` 0→6. Restore proven **by state**: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean, blob back to `ae52b1d01`.
- **The stale-`dist` hazard addressed by argument**: the pin imports `./ChartRenderer` and `./AdvancedChartImpl` relatively and the root vitest config aliases every workspace specifier to `src`, so the mutated source **is** the resolved module.
- ✅ `packages/core/src/utils/chart-presentation.ts` **untouched** — `seriesPresentation` already forwards both keys, so the dispatch's "say so explicitly if you touch it" clause resolved to *not needed*.
- **Two gates NOT MEASURED with stated preconditions**, and the first carries a specific argument rather than a shrug: `check:doc-snippets` compiles documented TS blocks, the three changed `.mdx` lines are `193/194/198`, and the fences in that region are `162-179` and `200-216` ⇒ this diff changes no compiled block. `check:eager-closure` has no `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` to weigh and the diff adds no import. ✅
- **Lint narrowing** carries all three legs, including the invariance argument (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`; the only repo matches are two RuleTester fixtures).

**⭐ Out-of-scope finding declined for a measured reason, not a scope reflex.** objectui#8157 — the radar mark hard-codes `fillOpacity={0.6}` and never calls the presentation helper, so authored `opacity`, `dashArray` **and the whole comparison treatment** are inert on radar for every variant. It was ⛔ not folded in because repairing it would **newly mute existing comparison radar series** (`0.6` → the helper's non-bar/non-area default `0.5`) — a visible change to already-drawn charts that wants its own decision. ⇒ declining because the fix has an **unbudgeted visible consequence** is a better reason than "out of scope", and it is the same care that produced the bar/scatter default fix above.

## Verdict

**PASS.** No Clause-② carrier is owed. ⛔ **Not landing yet** — CI has just started: **32** enumerated against `total_count: 32`, **10 `in_progress`** (`Lint`, Test shards 1–4, `Type Check`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `README Export Check`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Skill Example Check`, `Live E2E`), **zero failures**. ⚠️ `Lint` is unread and this seat will ⛔ not flip ready without it. `Live E2E` will fail; its signature will be matched against objectstack#16186's before it is stood down.
